I was okay with DMing until I had a great DM. Now I'm a big fan. Gotta say I still slightly prefer playing, but doing DM right is quite a lot of fun. Here are some of the things he taught me.

1 - When speaking as a PC, use voices. Use personality. It's fine to exaggerate stereotypes and be a bit comical. Have fun with it and your players will also.

2 - Be organized. Nothing takes the fun out of DMing like worrying about keeping track of combat and other details. I use cards for combat order--everyone writes their initiative roll on them, and each combat we make new ones. After someone's turn is over, move to the next card. Very simple. Also, it helps to have quick and easy stat blocks at the ready.

3 - Don't forget to give players freedom to use the Rule of Cool. Nothing livens up a session like letting a player do something that's just ridiculous enough to work. Give it a reasonable roll to succeed, but fudge it a bit if you need to. If it's something for flair that doesn't really affect the numerical balance of the game, let it go. As a DM, you have a tendency to want to apply rules and be 'logical' about 'what would really happen' but keep in mind that all your views on 'what would really happen' are based on your personal experience and may be wrong, and more importantly, don't fucking matter. Let the players be awesome and everyone will have more fun for it.

In high school, I was super-religious and very impressionable. My best friend thought he was being oppressed by demons, that they would follow him and appear to him in his room at night. One night, we were in a church lock-in and after everyone went to sleep we were still up listening to The Deftones on his discman. It was so heavy and angry. I loved it but we both felt guilty for listening to it because we thought it could open ourselves to demonic attack. After that we both went to the bathroom because we could talk louder in there without disturbing anyone. He started telling me this story about how he was into the Occult before he came to our Christian school, and while he was recounting a story about how he thought Satan was following him his eyes rolled into the back of his head and he fell to the ground and started convulsing heavily. Then I heard voices coming out of his mouth that didn't sound like him at all. I asked who I was talking to and I heard a scary voice that sounded like it was speaking another language. I tried commanding the spirits in the name of Jesus and prayed. I didn't know what else to do. I was terrified he would hurt me because his body convulsions were quite violent and I was alone in this bathroom with him. Eventually he snapped out of it and acted very confused and he didn't seem to remember anything that had just happened. Later that week he told me he was being visited by a demon named Deceit. While he was on the phone with me telling me this, he said the demon was there and he could see its eyes. Then it left. Right then the light bulb in my room blew out and he was terrified it was after me then. The following week after that I was on a missions trip in Monterrey, Mexico with my church and a bunch of youth group kids and I went up this huge hill to look out over the city one night. While we were up there I freaked out. I thought this demon Deceit was after me. I started making a big scene and crying and then I blacked out. I came to what seemed like a couple minutes later, but my friends told me it had been 45 minutes and that strange voices were coming out of my mouth. They were all afraid to even look at me. They said they had tried to perform an exorcism and it went away after they had been praying for a long time. I have never felt more afraid in my entire life. I experienced all of this as if it was very real and I was a wreck for months after that. I have since been diagnosed with bi-polar disorder and I have gained a lot of understanding about myself. I am also an atheist. The mind can do terrible things to trick you, especially when influenced by the power of belief. I still get upset even thinking about this experience.

TL:DR I thought my friend and I were being attacked and possessed by demons.

You were demon possessed and yet you are still an atheist?

What?
No. Demons aren't real. I believed very deeply in those things back then and my experience felt very real. I didn't become an atheist until I was in my late 20s.

tl;dr My last kidney stone episode that lasted over a week. Drink plenty of damn water, people.

Two weeks ago tomorrow, I woke up early in the morning with severe pain in my right abdominal area. After a few minutes of thinking it would pass, I started to wonder if it was my appendix. I starting mentally freaking out and then remembering the pain to be exactly like the pain I had 8 years ago that turned out to be a kidney stone likely a result of a UTI they informed me I had. Once I started vomiting, that was my cue to get to the ER. I was admitted, given my morphine, and then sent home presuming I would pass the stone on my own. The first one I had 8 years ago passed within hours, surely this one would be the same. NOPE. I spent Saturday and Sunday relaxing hoping it would pass and straining my piss. Sunday night rolls around and my pain killers are doing nothing. I'm in and out of cold chills and vomiting. I was able to get into my PCP first thing Monday morning, and he ordered a CT scan. If the sucker was too big, we'd have to then take action. My CT scan is scheduled for later that afternoon, but by this point, I can't keep any food or medicine down and in writhing pain. Second ER visit.

A little while later, I get the results that the stone is about 4mm with a second smaller stone about 1mm. Not huge but could also cause problems. I also find out I have a 4cm cyst on my left ovary. I didn't know what that meant and the ER doctor told me when I my husband was out on a phone call, so I just started internally worrying that something was wrong. I have an ultrasound next week to follow-up on that, but I hear it's common and typically nothing to worry about.

After the second visit, my parents stop by to see how I'm doing. My mom is a nurse, and after seeing me just miserable in pain and getting sick, she's like, nope, you can't keep on like this. So back to the ER we go. I'm admitted to the hospital this time. After another two days of not being able to eat and still vomiting and therefore not being able to take non-IV medication, my urologist wants to do surgery because the stone wasn't moving down my kidney like he'd hoped. Yes, get this fucker out. Surgery was last Wednesday afternoon, and I was scared. I knew it was a basic procedure, but I hadn't been in the hospital since I had my tonsils out at 5. It was so hard leaving my husband too. I could see the worry in his eyes, but he tried to stay strong.

Surgery went great. I had a stent put in. I was able to go home from the hospital late Wednesday night. Last Saturday I could take out my stent. Imagine a 12" coffee stirrer with another 12" of fishing line hanging out of your whowho dilly for 3 days. It was so painful to have that all up there irritating the area that just underwent surgery. I knew it was going to be easy to remove because I'd read up a bit...took about 10 seconds or so, but it was still pretty uncomfortable. The pain is all gone within 30 minutes, and I'm stoked because I FINALLY have relief. Then another hour or two passes and pain worse than I had with the actual kidney stone hits me. Again, I start sort of worrying it's another stone. My kidney is spasming constantly and was inflamed from the stent removal. I pop some pain killers and just hope for the best. They kicked in and within 3 hours, most of the pain had subsided. I recovered mostly by Monday, but then Wednesday rolls around and more pain...it's that other damn stone. It passed by late Wednesday afternoon thankfully. Kidney stones are just the worst.
